title: The rise of the emoji
paragraphs: Happy, angry, amazed - these are some of the emotions we like to express these days when we‘re sending a message on our smartphones! That’s why many of us now add little pictures to our texts to brighten up someone‘s mobile screen but we’re also using them as a quick way of telling someone how we‘re feeling. Yes, emojis have become a vital tool for communication.

Let’s clear one thing up first - there are emojis and emoticons. The latter are little images made using normal keys on a keyboard. For example, a colon, two dots, followed by the curved line of a close brackets is a ‘smiley face‘. But as technology has become more sophisticated, pre-made images have been created that can be simply added to your messages, which is great!

The emoji was first invented in Japan in the late 1990s and the word ’emoji‘ comes from the Japanese words for ’picture‘ and ’character‘. The number of different images has dramatically increased since then and now we have a picture for every mood or situation.

So now we have the option to give this new creation the visual ’thumbs-up‘ but have you thought (puzzled face) why we’ve become so addicted to using emojis? Professor Vyv Evans, has written a book called ‘The Emoji Code‘ - he says “increasingly, what we‘re finding is that digital communication is taking over from certain aspects of face-to-face interaction... one of the reasons emojis are so interesting is that they really do enable us to express our emotional selves much more effectively.” So emojis are a sort of substitute for the visual signals or non-verbal cues we normally give when we speak to someone face-to-face.

Another advantage of emojis is that they are an international language - they don‘t use words but tell a message in pictorial form so they can be easily interpreted whatever your native language. However, the emojis you send need some thought as they can sometimes be misinterpreted - if a friend sends you an emoji of a hammer, you may think he is angry when really he is saying he has hurt himself or he is clumsy!

Emojis are a good way for showing empathy - they are a virtual hug or a flirtatious tease. But as linguist Neil Cohn says, “to many, emoji are an exciting evolution of the way we communicate; to others, they are linguistic Armageddon.” It does show there is a lot more to our communication than words alone but does this mean the decline in traditional writing?

vocabulary.example: She expressed her emotions through art.
vocabulary.translation: 她通过艺术表达自己的情感。

vocabulary.entry: brighten up [phr.] /ˈbraɪtən ʌp/ 使明亮；使开心
vocabulary.example: A smile brightens up a person‘s face.
vocabulary.translation: 微笑使人的脸庞明亮起来。

vocabulary.example: She sent a heart emoji to show her love.
vocabulary.translation: 她发了一个心形表情符号来表达她的爱。

vocabulary.entry: emoticon [n.] /ɪˈməʊtɪkɒn/ 表情符号（由键盘字符组成）
vocabulary.example: The smiley face emoticon 🙂 is made with a colon and a close bracket.
vocabulary.translation: 笑脸表情符号🙂是由一个冒号和一个右括号组成的。

vocabulary.example: Modern smartphones are sophisticated devices.
vocabulary.translation: 现代智能手机是精密的设备。

vocabulary.example: The population has increased dramatically.
vocabulary.translation: 人口显著增加了。

vocabulary.entry: thumbs-up [n.] /ˌθʌmz ˈʌp/ 竖起大拇指；赞同
vocabulary.example: The project received a thumbs-up from the manager.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目得到了经理的认可。

vocabulary.example: Honey can be used as a substitute for sugar.
vocabulary.translation: 蜂蜜可以用作糖的替代品。

vocabulary.example: Body language is a form of non-verbal communication.
vocabulary.translation: 肢体语言是一种非语言交流形式。

vocabulary.example: She took her cue from her friend and stood up.
vocabulary.translation: 她收到朋友的暗示后站了起来。

vocabulary.example: The book has a pictorial history of the city.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书有这座城市的历史图画。

vocabulary.example: It‘s difficult to interpret his silence.
vocabulary.translation: 很难理解他的沉默。

vocabulary.example: Spanish is her native language.
vocabulary.translation: 西班牙语是她的母语。

vocabulary.example: His comments were misinterpreted by the media.
vocabulary.translation: 他的评论被媒体误解了。

vocabulary.example: She has great empathy for people in need.
vocabulary.translation: 她对有需要的人有很强的共情能力。

vocabulary.example: The game creates a virtual world for players.
vocabulary.translation: 这款游戏为玩家创造了一个虚拟世界。

vocabulary.example: She gave him a flirtatious smile.
vocabulary.translation: 她向他抛了一个媚眼。

vocabulary.example: His comment was meant as a tease, not an insult.
vocabulary.translation: 他的评论是戏弄，不是侮辱。

vocabulary.example: The linguist studies how languages evolve.
vocabulary.translation: 这位语言学家研究语言如何演变。

vocabulary.example: The evolution of the internet has changed our lives.
vocabulary.translation: 互联网的演变改变了我们的生活。

vocabulary.entry: Armageddon [n.] /ˌɑːməˈɡedən/ 大灾难 (圣经术语；比喻)
vocabulary.example: Some people see climate change as an environmental Armageddon.
vocabulary.translation: 一些人认为气候变化是一场环境大灾难。

vocabulary.example: There has been a decline in traditional letter writing.
vocabulary.translation: 传统信件写作有所衰落。

vocabulary.entry: take over [phr.] /teɪk ˈəʊvə/ 取代；接管
vocabulary.example: Digital media has taken over from print in many areas.
vocabulary.translation: 数字媒体在许多领域已经取代了印刷媒体。

vocabulary.example: The new software enables users to edit videos easily.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新软件使用户能够轻松编辑视频。

vocabulary.entry: be addicted to [phr.] /biː əˈdɪktɪd tuː/ 沉迷于；对……上瘾
vocabulary.example: Many teenagers are addicted to their phones.
vocabulary.translation: 许多青少年沉迷于手机。

sentences.english: Happy, angry, amazed - these are some of the emotions we like to express these days when we‘re sending a message on our smartphones!
sentences.chinese: 开心、生气、惊讶——这些是我们如今在智能手机上发消息时喜欢表达的一些情绪！

sentences.english: That’s why many of us now add little pictures to our texts to brighten up someone‘s mobile screen but we’re also using them as a quick way of telling someone how we‘re feeling.
sentences.chinese: 这就是为什么我们很多人现在会在信息中添加小图片来点亮别人的手机屏幕，而且我们也把它们当作一种快速告诉别人我们感受的方式。

sentences.english: Yes, emojis have become a vital tool for communication.
sentences.chinese: 没错，表情符号已经成为了一种重要的交流工具。

sentences.english: Let’s clear one thing up first - there are emojis and emoticons.
sentences.chinese: 我们首先要弄清楚一件事——有表情符号（emojis）和表情符号（由键盘字符组成的）（emoticons）。

sentences.english: The latter are little images made using normal keys on a keyboard.
sentences.chinese: 后者是用键盘上的普通按键组成的小图像。

sentences.english: For example, a colon, two dots, followed by the curved line of a close brackets is a ‘smiley face‘.
sentences.chinese: 例如，一个冒号（:），两个点，再加上右括号的曲线（）组成一个“笑脸”。

sentences.english: But as technology has become more sophisticated, pre-made images have been created that can be simply added to your messages, which is great!
sentences.chinese: 但是随着技术变得越来越复杂精密，预先制作好的图像可以被简单地添加到你的消息中，这太棒了！

sentences.english: The emoji was first invented in Japan in the late 1990s and the word ’emoji‘ comes from the Japanese words for ’picture‘ and ’character‘.
sentences.chinese: 表情符号最早是在20世纪90年代末在日本发明的，“emoji”这个词来自日语中表示“图片”和“字符”的词。

sentences.english: The number of different images has dramatically increased since then and now we have a picture for every mood or situation.
sentences.chinese: 从那以后，图像的数量大幅地增加了，现在我们每种情绪或情况都有对应的图片。

sentences.english: So now we have the option to give this new creation the visual ’thumbs-up‘ but have you thought (puzzled face) why we’ve become so addicted to using emojis?
sentences.chinese: 所以现在我们可以选择给这个新事物一个视觉上的“点赞”，但是你有没有想过（疑惑的表情）为什么我们会如此沉迷于使用表情符号呢？

sentences.english: Professor Vyv Evans, has written a book called ‘The Emoji Code‘ - he says “increasingly, what we‘re finding is that digital communication is taking over from certain aspects of face-to-face interaction... one of the reasons emojis are so interesting is that they really do enable us to express our emotional selves much more effectively.”
sentences.chinese: 维夫·埃文斯教授写了一本名为《表情符号密码》的书——他说：“我们发现，数字交流正在逐渐越来越多地取代某些面对面的交流……表情符号如此有趣的原因之一是，它们确实能让我们更有效地表达我们的情绪。”

sentences.english: So emojis are a sort of substitute for the visual signals or non-verbal cues we normally give when we speak to someone face-to-face.
sentences.chinese: 所以表情符号是我们在面对面和别人交谈时通常给出的视觉信号或非语言暗示的一种替代品。

sentences.english: Another advantage of emojis is that they are an international language - they don‘t use words but tell a message in pictorial form so they can be easily interpreted whatever your native language.
sentences.chinese: 表情符号的另一个优点是它们是一种国际语言——它们不使用文字，而是以图画的形式传达信息，所以无论你的母语是什么，它们都很容易被理解。

sentences.english: However, the emojis you send need some thought as they can sometimes be misinterpreted - if a friend sends you an emoji of a hammer, you may think he is angry when really he is saying he has hurt himself or he is clumsy!
sentences.chinese: 然而，你发送的表情符号需要斟酌，因为它们有时可能会被误解——如果一个朋友给你发送一个锤子的表情符号，你可能会认为他生气了，而实际上他是说他弄伤了自己或者他很笨拙！

sentences.english: Emojis are a good way for showing empathy - they are a virtual hug or a flirtatious tease.
sentences.chinese: 表情符号是表达共情的好方法——它们就像一个虚拟的拥抱或者一个轻浮的挑逗。

sentences.english: But as linguist Neil Cohn says, “to many, emoji are an exciting evolution of the way we communicate; to others, they are linguistic Armageddon.”
sentences.chinese: 但是正如语言学家尼尔·科恩所说：“对很多人来说，表情符号是我们交流方式的一次令人兴奋的进化；对另一些人来说，它们是语言的大灾难。”

sentences.english: It does show there is a lot more to our communication than words alone but does this mean the decline in traditional writing?
sentences.chinese: 这确实表明我们的交流不仅仅是文字，但这是否同时也意味着传统写作的衰落呢？
